source.title: Parallel organization of functionally segregated circuits linking basal ganglia and cortex.

confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily replicated primate anatomical/physiological synthesis that is the explicit translation target named in the ARC-110 title. Source quality is very high (foundational review, thousands of confirmations). The mapping to ARC-110 is direct at the architectural level (separate motor / associative / limbic channels each with their own cortico-striatal-pallidal-thalamic re-entrant loop). Confidence is held below 0.9 only because the paper grounds the *organisational claim* (the loops exist and are segregated) and does not itself test the *functional consequence* ARC-110 asserts -- that running selection through separate channels relieves the single-arena F-dominance ceiling. That second step is REE's hypothesis, not Alexander et al.'s finding.
failure_signatures: Alexander et al. describe the loops as anatomically segregated at the macro scale but explicitly leave open the degree of functional integration vs. isolation -- a strict no-cross-talk reading is stronger than the paper licenses.

The framework is descriptive anatomy/physiology in primate; it does not demonstrate that segregation per se changes which channel wins a committed selection, so it cannot by itself confirm the MECH-439 artefact hypothesis.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Five (and more generally multiple) cortico-basal ganglia-thalamocortical circuits -- including a motor, an oculomotor, dorsolateral-prefrontal (associative), and limbic/anterior-cingulate circuit -- are organised as parallel, anatomically and functionally segregated re-entrant loops, each passing through its own territory of striatum, pallidum/nigra, and thalamus before returning to its originating cortical field.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-110's committed-action selector should be decomposed into N>=3 parallel loop channels (motor=F, associative=dACC+lPFC, limbic=OFC+liking) each owning its own eligibility-and-gate and arbitrated only AFTER within-loop competition, rather than collapsing every channel into one shared E3 selection arena where dACC/lPFC/OFC enter as additive biases. Alexander/DeLong/Strick is the named functional analogue for that decomposition.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper establishes that the loops are anatomically separable, not that selecting through separate loops removes the F-dominance conversion ceiling (MECH-439). REE maps the *architecture*; the *F-cannot-drown-limbic* benefit is an REE hypothesis that this paper motivates but does not test. ARC-110 itself flags the translation as FUNCTIONAL, not anatomical mimicry, so over-reading anatomical segregation as proof of the selection benefit would be a transfer error.
mapping.source_context: Review/synthesis of primate (macaque) tract-tracing and single-unit electrophysiology; macro-circuit anatomy and topography, not a behaving-agent selection experiment.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality near-ceiling (canonical review). Mapping fidelity high for the architectural decomposition but not for the functional selection-benefit claim. Transfer risk moderate: primate macro-anatomy -> a learned RL selection head is a structural analogy, and ARC-110 deliberately scopes it as functional rather than homological, which contains the risk.
